title: Starting on bass drum: carnival kazoo band and Willie Parker
summary: He started on bass drum, leading a kazoo band on carnival day, then was hired by Willie Parker for his first real brass-band parade.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: No, right off there, no, I really don't remember. It's been quite a while. Yeah. See, because the facts like this, I hadn't took very long to start it out playing bass drum. Well, the facts, that's how I started playing drums, from a bass drum. I used to play with a little carnival band on carnival day. I had a little group, fellas with a 10-second-a-lones. Mm-hmm. And I had made up my band on carnival day. We used to play for different clubs, the Square Deal Club. We played for them one year. And from different clubs after that, we used to have to play the carnival parades like that. Girls dressed in baby dolls, you know. Mm-hmm. We used to play, we had about eight kazoots and two drums. That must have been set. Oh, it was, really. All the guys who had me playing bass drum on the street on carnival day. And an old fella by the name of Willie Parker. Old guy, he played bass drum. He used to play baritone a long time ago. So he decided to hire me to play a carnival day with him. And that was for the club down in the Arabi club. That was my first carnival parade. I played with a brass band. And it was an old man, I recall one of the old men that was playing, he's dead now. Oh, he called a play drum on by the name of him. Can't think of his name. Probably will come to me. I know Wooden Joe was one of them, he was the trumpet player. And Joe liked the way I played drums. So, from then on, I used to play this band with Willie Parker's band. I think that's where your record band first started. Willie Parker, the first one that started your record band. Because I remember they used to have rehearsals at his house. I was a kid then.

He's the first man who brought me on the street of playing bass drum. Because he liked the way I played UCS on carnival day like that. And he'd take a life in town. And he brought me, and I thought it was a lot of money. I made ten dollars to play a parade. Walked from the slaughterhouse all the way up to the Leith Sake and St. Charles Street up there. Man, that was a walk. Well, it didn't affect me. I was pretty young. It didn't work in my life. I got a big kick out of it. Waste time playing in a real brass band. I played two years for those people with that same band.
